title: World Bank RCT in Benin City: six weeks of Microsoft Copilot (GPT-4) English tutoring in nine public schools raises assessment scores 0.31 SD
summary: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125: teacher-guided after-school Copilot (GPT-4) sessions, June-July 2024, Benin City; 0.31 SD overall, 0.23 SD in English; 657 treated, 671 control.
account: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125 (May 2025) is by De Simone, Tiberti, Barron Rodriguez, Manolio, Mosuro and Dikoru. It evaluates a six-week after-school program run in June and July 2024 in nine public schools in Benin City, Nigeria, chosen for their computer labs. First-year senior secondary students, typically 15 years old, who expressed interest were randomized: 657 to treatment and 671 to control. Of these, 422 and 337 finished the final assessment. Treated students attended up to two 90-minute sessions a week (twelve in total). They used Microsoft Copilot, powered by GPT-4 at the time, as a virtual English tutor in curriculum-aligned activities guided by teachers. The paper reports a 0.31 standard deviation improvement on an assessment covering English, AI knowledge and digital skills, and 0.23 SD on English. It equates the gains to 1.5 to 2 years of business-as-usual schooling. Effects were larger for female students and those with higher initial performance. The World Bank blog of 9 January 2025 describes the gain as about 0.3 SD. The paper gives months, not days.
purpose: Copilot was used as a virtual tutor to improve English learning outcomes. The measured gain is that purpose.

data.answer:
World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125: teacher-guided after-school Copilot (GPT-4) sessions, June-July 2024, Benin City; 0.31 SD overall, 0.23 SD in English; 657 treated, 671 control.

The reported 0.31-SD endpoint combines English, AI knowledge, and digital skills; the English-only estimate is 0.23 SD. Only 759 of 1,328 randomized students completed the final assessment, so differential attrition needs scrutiny. The intervention combines extra instruction, teachers, computers, and AI, and school-year equivalents are a conversion rather than directly observed years of learning.

fields.account: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125 (May 2025) is by De Simone, Tiberti, Barron Rodriguez, Manolio, Mosuro and Dikoru. It evaluates a six-week after-school program run in June and July 2024 in nine public schools in Benin City, Nigeria, chosen for their computer labs. First-year senior secondary students, typically 15 years old, who expressed interest were randomized: 657 to treatment and 671 to control. Of these, 422 and 337 finished the final assessment. Treated students attended up to two 90-minute sessions a week (twelve in total). They used Microsoft Copilot, powered by GPT-4 at the time, as a virtual English tutor in curriculum-aligned activities guided by teachers. The paper reports a 0.31 standard deviation improvement on an assessment covering English, AI knowledge and digital skills, and 0.23 SD on English. It equates the gains to 1.5 to 2 years of business-as-usual schooling. Effects were larger for female students and those with higher initial performance. The World Bank blog of 9 January 2025 describes the gain as about 0.3 SD. The paper gives months, not days.

fields.title: World Bank RCT in Benin City: six weeks of Microsoft Copilot (GPT-4) English tutoring in nine public schools raises assessment scores 0.31 SD
fields.headline: Microsoft Copilot tutoring lifts Benin City scores by 0.31 SD

fields.account: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11125 (May 2025) is by De Simone, Tiberti, Barron Rodriguez, Manolio, Mosuro and Dikoru. It evaluates a six-week after-school program run in June and July 2024 in nine public schools in Benin City, Nigeria, chosen for their computer labs. First-year senior secondary students, typically 15 years old, who expressed interest were randomized: 657 to treatment and 671 to control. Of these, 422 and 337 finished the final assessment. Treated students attended up to two 90-minute sessions a week (twelve in total). They used Microsoft Copilot, powered by GPT-4 at the time, as a virtual English tutor in curriculum-aligned activities guided by teachers. The paper reports a 0.31 standard deviation improvement on an assessment covering English, AI knowledge and digital skills, and 0.23 SD on English. It equates the gains to 1.5 to 2 years of business-as-usual schooling. Effects were larger for female students and those with higher initial performance. The World Bank blog of 9 January 2025 describes the gain as about 0.3 SD. The paper gives months, not days.

produced_by: A freely available LLM (Copilot on GPT-4) requiring only student registration
Curriculum-aligned prompts and activities guided by teachers in school computer labs
Student-level randomization among volunteers in nine schools with computer labs
must_hold: Working computer labs and internet access
Attendance (the paper reports gains rising with days attended)
